scenarios.name: Hero Section Display
scenarios.description: Verify the hero section displays product name, tagline, and primary CTAs prominently above the fold

steps.description: Navigate to the MirDB homepage URL
steps.context: User lands on the page for the first time

steps.description: Check that the product name 'MirDB', tagline, and value proposition are visible without scrolling
steps.context: First viewport should contain essential branding elements

steps.description: Confirm 'Get Started' button and 'View on GitHub' link are present and functional
steps.context: Primary and secondary call-to-action buttons should be prominent

test_cases.input: Load homepage and check for 'MirDB' product name in hero section
test_cases.expected: Product name 'MirDB' is displayed prominently in the hero section

test_cases.input: Check for tagline text communicating persistent memcached value proposition
test_cases.expected: Tagline is visible and communicates the core value proposition (e.g., 'Persistent memcached, powered by Rust')

test_cases.input: Click 'Get Started' button in hero section
test_cases.expected: User is navigated to the Getting Started section of the page
User is directed to the MirDB source code repository

scenarios.name: Features Section Content
scenarios.description: Verify the features section displays key MirDB features with clear explanations

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the features section of the homepage
steps.context: User wants to understand MirDB's capabilities

steps.description: Check that all key features are displayed: memcached compatibility, persistence, LSM tree architecture, Rust performance
steps.context: Features should be clearly organized with icons and descriptions

steps.description: Confirm each feature has a title and brief description explaining what it does and why it matters
steps.context: Descriptions should be informative but concise

test_cases.input: Check features section for 'memcached protocol compatibility' feature
test_cases.expected: Feature is displayed with icon, title, and description explaining compatibility with existing memcached clients
Feature is displayed explaining data persistence with SSTables and durability across restarts

test_cases.input: Check features section for 'LSM tree architecture' feature
test_cases.expected: Feature is displayed explaining the LSM tree storage architecture and its benefits

test_cases.input: Check features section for 'Rust performance' feature
test_cases.expected: Feature is displayed explaining the performance and memory safety benefits of Rust implementation

test_cases.input: Verify each feature has an accompanying icon
test_cases.expected: All features display with visual icons that represent their functionality

scenarios.name: Getting Started Section
scenarios.description: Verify installation instructions and basic usage examples are provided

steps.description: Scroll to or navigate to the getting started section
steps.context: User wants to install and try MirDB

steps.description: Check that step-by-step installation instructions are provided
steps.context: Instructions should be clear and complete

steps.description: Confirm code examples for basic operations are present with syntax highlighting
steps.context: Examples should cover SET, GET, DELETE operations

test_cases.input: Check Getting Started section for installation instructions
test_cases.expected: Step-by-step installation instructions are displayed in a code block
A basic configuration example showing TOML format is provided
Instructions for connecting to MirDB using a memcached client are provided

scenarios.name: Code Examples with Operations
scenarios.description: Verify code examples for SET, GET, DELETE operations are provided with expected responses

steps.description: Find the section containing memcached protocol code examples

steps.description: Check that SET command example is provided with syntax and expected response
steps.context: SET command format and STORED response should be documented

steps.description: Check that GET command example is provided with syntax and expected response

steps.description: Check that DELETE command example is provided with syntax and expected response
steps.context: DELETE command format and DELETED response should be documented

test_cases.input: Check for SET command example in code examples section
test_cases.expected: SET command example with memcached protocol format (e.g., 'set key 0 0 5\r\nvalue\r\n') and expected 'STORED' response is displayed
GET command example with memcached protocol format (e.g., 'get key') and expected VALUE/END response is displayed
DELETE command example with memcached protocol format (e.g., 'delete key') and expected 'DELETED' response is displayed

test_cases.input: Verify code blocks have syntax highlighting
test_cases.expected: All code examples are displayed with appropriate syntax highlighting for readability

test_cases.input: Test copy-to-clipboard functionality on code examples
test_cases.expected: Code examples can be copied to clipboard with a single click using copy button
